title: How to specify multiple "named" OpenAPI examples with additional responses on the router?
body:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.

- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel


class ErrorSchema(BaseModel):
    error_type: str
    message: str
    detail: str | None = None


class APIErrorResponseSchema(BaseModel):
    error: ErrorSchema

    model_config = {
        "json_schema_extra": {
            "examples": [
                {
                    "error": {
                         "error_type": "database_connection_error",
                         "message": "Database could not be accessed",
                         "detail": "Database query timed out"
                    }
                }
            ]
        }
    }


router = APIRouter(responses={
    500: {
        "model": APIErrorResponseSchema,
        "description": "Internal Server Error",
    },
}


@router.post("/here")
async def post_here():
    func_that_can_raise_HTTException_with_500()
```


### Description

I'd like to thoroughly document all possible responses of my endpoints - including meaningful examples for additional responses defined on the router level.

With the code above, Swagger/Redoc correctly render the 500 Internal Server Error with the example specified in the model_config of `APIErrorResponseSchema`.

I'd like to globally specify multiple different _named_ examples as possible via the OpenAPI examples (see https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/schema-extra-example/#body-with-multiple-examples). Globally, because I'd like to reuse the specified additional responses across multiple routers.

How can I achieve this, when these additional responses are provided via the `responses` key on the router itself?

Additionally, is it possible to extend these examples specified on the router for a single path operation? E.g. for a single path of a router, the 500 code should have another example.

### Operating System

Linux, Windows

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.115.12

### Pydantic Version

2.11.5

### Python Version

3.12.6

### Additional Context

_No response_
